task_title: Diagnose a recovery-loop and propose a bounded fix
output:
(a) Root cause
`reconcileStrandedAssignedIssues` treats assigned work with no active run as stranded and keeps enqueueing recovery wakes. Deliberate pause (weekly rate-limit, fixed resume) is not treated as a terminal non-invoke state, so the same 13 leadership primaries stay “stranded,” every sweep retries them, and ~986/day die with “Agent is not invokable (paused)”—a tight detect→wake→fail loop, not real recovery.

(b) One product rule
If the assignee is paused (or otherwise non-invokable by design), do not schedule stranded-issue recovery wakes for their assignments until they are invokable again; hold that work under the pause as the acknowledged stop.

(c) Invariants
(1) Unpaused agents and other work still recover and run. (2) Only real stops apply—planned pause is intentional; crash/OOM-style stranding still recovers. (3) No loop: once paused assignees are out of the recovery set, the ~110/hr hammer ends until resume.

judgeDetail.rationale: Correctly roots the cause in recovery re-invoking deliberately-paused agents and fixes it by excluding paused assignees from the sweep until resume, with a valid, explicit walk-through of all three invariants.

task_title: Diagnose the three compounding defects in the restart race
output:
Root cause — three compounding defects

1. Restart race / no single-instance guard  
launchd KeepAlive re-execs the start script the moment `pnpm dev` exits while the old embedded-Postgres postmaster and detached workspace-runtime (port 13100) are still up. The script only frees 3100 and has no lock, so you get postmaster.pid / port-in-use failures.  
Fix: single-instance lock + full cleanup (Postgres + 13100 and any other owned ports/PIDs) before start; throttle KeepAlive until cleanup succeeds.

2. Ungraceful SIGTERM  
The handler neither drains in-flight runs nor kills detached children before exit, so orphans and half-dead workspaces survive the restart.  
Fix: on SIGTERM, stop accepting work, drain/cancel in-flight runs with a bounded timeout, then kill the process group (including detached children), then exit.

3. Over-aggressive orphan reaping  
`reapOrphanedRuns()` runs at startup with stale-threshold 0, so every row still marked `running` is immediately `process_lost`—including runs that would have finished or been reattached after a clean handoff.  
Fix: require a real stale threshold (and/or heartbeat/lease check) before marking `process_lost`; only reap when the owner PID/lease is gone past that window.

judgeDetail.rationale: All three compounding defects are cleanly separated with specific, correct fixes—single-instance lock plus ordered old-PG/port-13100 teardown, bounded SIGTERM drain plus process-group kill of detached children, and a real stale/lease threshold before reaping.
